final_answer:
>>> When an mRNA vaccine is injected, it is delivered into the muscle cells via a lipid nanoparticle (LNPs) carrier. These nanoparticles protect the mRNA from degradation and facilitate its entry into the cell.  
>>> Once inside the cell, the mRNA is released into the cytoplasm. The cell's ribosomes read the mRNA sequence, which encodes a viral protein (e.g., the spike protein of SARS-CoV-2).  
>>> The ribosomes translate the mRNA into the viral protein, which is then displayed on the cell surface or processed for presentation to the immune system.  
>>> Dendritic cells (a type of antigen-presenting cell) detect the viral protein, engulf it, and present fragments of it to T-cells and B-cells.  
>>> Helper T-cells activate B-cells, which produce antibodies specific to the viral protein. Cytotoxic T-cells are also activated to destroy cells displaying the viral antigen.  
>>> Memory B-cells and T-cells are generated, providing long-term immunity. If the body encounters the actual virus later, these memory cells rapidly mount an immune response to neutralize it.  
>>> The mRNA is degraded by the cell’s enzymes after the protein is produced, ensuring it does not integrate into the genome or persist in the body.
